key_insight: Dream to Remember (D2R) continually adapts a frozen generalist robot policy to new tasks while preventing catastrophic forgetting by rehearsing prior behaviors through a frozen world model.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical continual-learning recipe for robotics that improves task adaptation without replay buffers, while preserving prior robot skills across sequential updates.
method: Freeze the base generalist policy and learn only a lightweight steering module.
Use a pretrained world model to generate imagined rollouts that rehearse earlier tasks.
Train new tasks in imagination when the world model is accurate enough; otherwise, train in the environment while the world model anchors past behavior.
evidence_signal: Across CALVIN, D2R raised average success from 63.7% to 74.8% over eight sequential tasks in imagination, while LoRA fine-tuning fell to 11.7%; it also retained prior performance on LIBERO and improved three real-robot Franka tasks.
watch_item: Performance depends on the fidelity of the frozen world model, so weak model predictions may limit optimization quality and shift training back to real-environment learning.
paper_title: Dream to Remember: Continual Steering of Generalist Robot Policies with World Models
